events.title: Kotlin 1.0 released
events.summary: JetBrains released Kotlin 1.0 on February 15, 2016 — the first stable version of the pragmatic JVM and Android language.
events.about: Kotlin 1.0 committed to backward compatibility for the language and standard library — safe for production Android and server code. Google later made Kotlin the preferred Android language. Null-safe types, data classes, and coroutines reduced boilerplate versus Java.

narrative.whyChosen: Kotlin 1.0 was the stability milestone that let enterprises bet on Kotlin beyond experiments.
narrative.whyImportant: It unlocked Google's Android pivot and proved JetBrains could ship a mainstream JVM language.
narrative.problemSolved: Preview Kotlin changed frequently; teams needed a stable 1.0 with long-term compatibility guarantees.

events.title: Zig programming language announced
events.summary: Andrew Kelley introduced Zig on February 8, 2016 — a systems language aiming to be a pragmatic, safer alternative to C with full C ABI compatibility.
events.about: Zig targets bare-metal, games, and compilers — manual memory, comptime execution, and no hidden control flow. It ships with a build system and cross-compilation toolchain. Developers reach for it when C's footguns and C++ complexity are too costly but Rust's borrow checker is too strict.

narrative.whyChosen: Zig reframed systems programming around explicit allocators, comptime, and C interop without a runtime.
narrative.whyImportant: It renewed interest in simple systems languages and influenced how newer toolchains think about builds and cross-compilation.
narrative.problemSolved: Kelley hit friction integrating C libraries in Go, memory bugs in C++, and Rust's learning curve while building a DAW.
